extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, university/college administrators, and state EPSCoR program staff preparing or considering applications to the U.S. DOE EPSCoR program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility information for institutions and investigators preparing proposals to the U.S. Department of Energy Established Program to Stimulate Competitive Research (DOE EPSCoR), which funds efforts to build sustainable, nationally competitive energy-related research capacity in designated jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional eligibility (follow NSF EPSCoR criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE EPSCoR currently follows the NSF EPSCoR eligibility criteria. Thus twenty-five states, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands are eligible to participate in the DOE EPSCoR program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be from one of the designated eligible jurisdictions. The page lists the eligible jurisdictions explicitly (Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Delaware, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Vermont, Virgin Islands, West Virginia, Wyoming).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research scope — energy-related and DOE-relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE EPSCoR is designed to enhance capabilities to conduct sustainable and nationally competitive energy-related research and welcomes applications for research spanning the range of program offices and topical areas covered by the Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address energy-related scientific or engineering research topics that align with DOE program offices and topical areas. The program has a strong science orientation but is not limited to a single discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose — capacity building and competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is a federal-state partnership designed to enhance the capabilities of designated states and territories to conduct sustainable and nationally competitive energy-related research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should aim to build or strengthen institutional research capacity and help the jurisdiction become more competitive nationally in energy-related science and engineering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required academic component — education and training
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong academic component including the education of graduate students or training of post-doctoral fellows is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must include substantive plans for graduate student education and/or postdoctoral training as part of project activities and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial participation encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial participation or leadership on grant applications is also welcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the academic/education component is required, involving industry partners—whether as participants or leaders—is permitted and encouraged where appropriate to the proposal objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: State/territory demonstrated commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE EPSCoR addresses its mission by fostering competitions for scientific and engineering research in states and territories that have demonstrated a commitment to develop their research bases and to improve the quality of science and engineering research conducted at their universities and colleges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible jurisdictions are expected to have shown institutional or state-level commitment to developing research capacity; proposals should be consistent with and supported by those commitments (e.g., state programs, matching support, institutional initiatives).
